newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open at new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open at new all-time high.

text.p: Australian shares surged at the open on Monday, the market reaching a new all-time high in the first 10 minutes of trade after U.S. inflation data triggered a strong rally on Wall Street on Friday.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 14.1 points higher at 2,350.9, eclipsing its previous all time high of 2,350.4 which was set in February 1994.
The December share price index was up 19 points at 2,378 and at a 27.1 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market rose across the board with gains by resource issues matching those by industrials.
After the strong open, shares pulled back from their early highs, the index so far setting an intra-day high of 2,352.1 in its first 45 minutes of trade.
"An initial flurry of buying pushed the market through the key 2,350 level, but since then it has pulled back convincingly," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said investors were awaiting an important announcement from regional banks Advance and St George after they requested that trading in their shares be halted.
"The market is expecting a merger," said Geoff Burrell, a director of Brisbane brokerage, Burrell and Co.
Dealers said Advance shares have been rising stongly since the beginning of September on market speculation the bank was seeking a merger with another Australian bank.
